newsitem.title: GREECE: SOCCER-MULTI-MILLION DOLLAR TEENAGER TIPPED FOR GREATNESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MULTI-MILLION DOLLAR TEENAGER TIPPED FOR GREATNESS.

text.p: Two outstanding individual goals in pre-season friendlies last week have left fans of Olympiakos of Piraeus feeling as if they had won the league title or the Cup final.

Both goals -- against Leicester City of England and Lazio of Italy -- came from the right foot of 17-year-old Ghanaian Peter Oforiquaye, who has just joined the Greek champions for the staggering sum of $4.0 million from first division Kalamata.

It is believed to be the second largest amount ever spent on a teenager's transfer after the $7.0 million Barcelona paid for then 18-year-old Ronaldo's signature when they prised him away from PSV Eindhoven last year.
And while Olympiakos, who have signed him on a five-year contract, have clearly taken a gamble on a player so young, everything he has done so far suggests they have made a very shrewd purchase.
Oforiquaye, who turned 17 in March, has been in Greece with Kalamata since he was 15, and while the cost of his tranfer is astonishing, that is not the only unusual aspect of the move.

Kalamata reportedly refused even bigger offers from Ajax, Bayern Munich and Anderlecht for his signature and dealt with Olympiakos in much the same way that a parent allows a son to leave home in the country to live with a more wordly-wise relative in the big city.
Kalamata president Stavros Papadoupoulos believes Oforiquaye is destined for greatness beyond Greece. But that is in the future and Olympiakos are the perfect stepping stone for now.

Oforiquaye himself is delighted with the move: "It is ideal for me. I wanted to stay in Greece and Olympiakos are the best team in the country. Perhaps it will be a stepping stone too to something else one day. But I am pleased to be part of their family."
Olympiakos president Socrates Kokkalis is absolutely delighted with his new young acquisition.

"Our first goal is for Olympiakos to get the best players in Greece and be the best team in Greece. Peter is destined for greatness. He is strong, tall, powerful and fast -- and he is still maturing and getting better."

He is extremely fast and has been timed at 11.0 seconds for the 100 metres -- a world class time for his age and quicker than some of the men who ran in the 100 at this week's world athletics championships in Athens.

Oforiquaye made his debut as a second half substitute for Olympiakos in a friendly against Leicester in Athens last week and caught the eye with a superbly taken individual goal two minutes from the end of a 3-1 victory.
Collecting the ball on the left-hand side of the penalty area, he took a couple of strides before unleashing an unstoppable drive into the top left-hand corner of the Leicester net from 18 metres.
He dedicated that goal to the Olympiakos fans. "That's my gift to them for the welcome they gave me," he said.
Last weekend in Rome he gave them another even though Olympiakos lost 3-2 to Lazio. The goal came in the second half when Oforiquaye turned and volleyed the ball home in one flowing movement.
Dusan Bayevic, Olympiakos's Yugoslav coach, is understandably cautious in his praise but can hardly contain his excitement at the find that has arrived on his doorstep.
"He still has much to learn and I believe he will become even better as time passes."
"There is no doubt he is potentially a great talent," Bayevic added. "I watched him throughout last season at Kalamata and I believe he can develop into a great player at Olympiakos."

Already nicknamed "The Black Panther" by the Greek media, many observers feel Oforiquaye could be the third great player to emerge from Africa after Eusebio -- the original Black Panther nearly four decades ago -- and George Weah more recently.
Born on March 21, 1980, he played briefly for Goldfields in Ghana before being snapped up by Kalamata, who also had six other Ghanaians on their books.
They nurtured him carefully for half a season before giving him his debut shortly after he turned 16 towards the end of the 1995-96 season.
He returned their faith with a goal on his debut and went on to play eight more matches, gaining in confidence and maturity in each one.
Last season he played 26 games and scored seven times from a position just behind the attacking pair.

He was in the Ghana team who finished fourth in the Under-20 World Cup in Malaysia this summer, and is set to play for Olympiakos in their European Cup preliminary round match against Mozyr of Belarus next week.
If Olympiakos come through the two legs of that encounter - as they should - they will come up against Europe's best over the next few months.
Despite Oforiquaye's tender years, they will be looking for something very special from their young multi-million dollar starlet.
